study_id: Dueñas-Jurado et al. - 2021 - New models for donor-recipient matching in lung transplantations

eligibility.Eligibility Rationale: The study analyzes adult lung transplant recipients using a neural network (non‑linear AI) to predict six‑month survival, published in a peer‑reviewed journal in 2021, thus meeting all inclusion criteria.

identification_methods.Sponsorship source: Spanish Ministry of Economy and Competitiveness (MINECO) and FEDER
identification_methods.Setting: Reina Sofia University Hospital, Cordoba, Spain (Intensive Care Unit and Lung Transplant Service)
identification_methods.Comments: Retrospective analysis of 404 lung transplants performed over 23 years.
identification_methods.Institution: Reina Sofia University Hospital, Cordoba, Spain
identification_methods.Address: Reina Sofia University Hospital, Cordoba, Spain
identification_methods.Dataset Source: Hospital records from the Lung Transplant Program at Reina Sofia University Hospital
identification_methods.Identification Notes: Included adult lung transplant recipients; excluded pediatric (<15 years) and combined/multi-organ transplants (>2 organs).
identification_methods.AI Model Architecture: Logistic Regression combined with Evolutionary Product‑Unit Neural Network (EPUNN)
identification_methods.Input Variables: Demographic, clinical and procedural variables of donors and recipients (e.g., age, sex, disease type, ventilation status, cause of donor death, ischemia time, transplant type, etc.)
identification_methods.Methods Notes: Used evolutionary algorithms and product‑unit neural networks; hybrid LR‑EPUNN model optimized for binary survival outcome at six months.

population.Inclusion criteria: Retrospective analysis of lung transplant recipients performed at Reina Sofía University Hospital between October 1993 and January 2016
population.Exclusion criteria: Pediatric recipients (<15 years) and combined or multi-organ transplants (more than two vital organs)
population.Population Notes: Single‑center cohort spanning 23 years; all transplants performed at the same hospital
population.Diagnosis: Recipient underlying disease categories included COPD, cystic fibrosis, pulmonary fibrosis, bronchiectasis and other respiratory diseases
population.Pre-transplant Support: Pre‑transplant status recorded (ambulatory, hospitalized, ICU) but percentages not reported
population.Ischemic Time: Cold ischemia time categorized (short, medium, long, very long) but no mean value reported

interventions_outcomes.Specific Algorithm Name: LRIPU (logistic regression using initial covariates and product units)
interventions_outcomes.Intervention Input Data Modality: Tabular clinical variables (donor and recipient characteristics)
interventions_outcomes.Temporal Handling: Static baseline data (variables collected at transplant)
interventions_outcomes.Interventions Notes: Hybrid model combining logistic regression with evolutionary product‑unit neural network (EPUNN) to optimize architecture and weights
interventions_outcomes.Outcomes Notes: Primary outcome is binary survival/non‑survival of the graft at six months post‑transplant
interventions_outcomes.Result data Notes: Model provides probability equation; no performance metrics (e.g., AUC, accuracy) reported
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome group: All 404 lung transplant recipients in the retrospective cohort
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Reporting: Model coefficients and probability equation; no quantitative performance reported
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Metric Definition: Probability of graft survival derived from logistic regression‑product unit model
interventions_outcomes.Primary Outcome Notes: Outcome focused on six‑month graft survival; no separate in‑hospital, 1‑year or late timepoint results provided
